title: Marketplace Refresh Kickoff (AWS + GCP) — Scope, Timeline, Owners
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Marketplace Listings Refresh (AWS + GCP)
Kickoff: scope, timeline, owners, and launch plan

Speaker notes:
- Objective today: align cross-functional owners on what we’re shipping, by when, and how we’ll pass review + reduce onboarding friction.
- This is not a deep dive on every SKU detail; we’ll leave with decision points + next meetings.


Slide 2 — Why we’re doing this
We’re refreshing marketplace packaging + onboarding to unblock enterprise procurement without losing developer-first onboarding.

Primary outcomes:
- More marketplace-sourced pipeline + faster procurement (POs, invoicing, committed spend)
- Clear SKU taxonomy aligned to Hosted API / Dedicated / Private + add-ons
- Security posture presented accurately + reviewer-ready documentation
- Purchase → entitlement → org linking is reliable, observable, and supportable

Speaker notes:
- Today: marketplace is working “enough” for some buyers, but we see friction at enterprise procurement + provisioning edges (entitlement delays, wrong org, region mismatch).


Slide 3 — Goals + non-goals
Goals (this project)
- Launch new SKUs (base + add-ons where applicable) with consistent naming across AWS/GCP + Console + internal billing
- Pass AWS/GCP marketplace listing + security reviews with updated evidence
- Improve buyer onboarding: entitlement activation time, clearer instructions, fewer tickets
- Enable field + CS: talk tracks, FAQ, mutual action plans, troubleshooting

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)
- Major inference runtime features unrelated to marketplace onboarding
- Full billing re-platform (we will do minimal changes required for new SKUs/metering)

Speaker notes:
- We will make necessary “glue” changes in billing/metering and Console, but we are not redesigning billing.


Slide 4 — Target buyers + primary use cases
Personas
- Procurement-led enterprise buyer: needs vendor/security packet, invoice-friendly spend, predictable contract terms
- Platform team: wants standard inference procurement across teams + central budgeting
- Developer/ML engineer: wants quick activation and clear docs

Primary purchase motions
- New customer: first contract via AWS/GCP Marketplace
- Existing customer: move spend to marketplace for consolidated cloud billing
- Expansion: add Dedicated capacity / Private deployment under marketplace procurement

Speaker notes:
- Marketplace buyers often have strict internal steps; our job is to remove ambiguity and delays.


Slide 5 — What’s changing (high-level)
1) Listings + copy refresh
- Updated value props, screenshots, categories/keywords
- Updated FAQs (esp. security + provisioning)

2) SKU + packaging refresh
- Base SKUs: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private
- Add-ons: compliance package, longer retention/observability, premium SLA (where applicable)
- Clear mapping to Redwood internal plans + entitlements

3) Security packet refresh
- Reviewer-ready attachments + evidence index, with correct disclaimers and NDA handling

4) Purchase → provisioning improvements
- Entitlement ingestion + idempotent processing
- Org linking wizard in Console + clear error states
- Region mapping clarity + mitigations for mismatches

Speaker notes:
- We’re treating “purchase-to-provision” as a product surface, not just ops glue.


Slide 6 — In-scope deliverables (checklist)
Marketplace
- AWS listing: updated long description, pricing table, keywords, screenshots, support links
- GCP listing: updated solution description, deployment steps, marketplace FAQs

Product + Eng
- Entitlement mapping layer (AWS/GCP SKU IDs → Redwood entitlement IDs)
- Webhook validation + audit logs for provisioning events
- Console UX: onboarding wizard + entitlement status display
- Billing: new plan codes + invoice descriptions aligned to SKUs

Security/Compliance
- Updated security packet (overview, encryption/logging, shared responsibility)
- Evidence index with owners + refresh cadence (SOC2 handling, pen test letters, diagrams)

Docs + Enablement
- Docs pages: AWS onboarding + GCP onboarding + FAQs + troubleshooting
- Sales/SE/CS enablement slides + talk tracks
- Support macros + escalation routing


Slide 7 — Workstreams + owners
Workstream A — SKU & Packaging
- DRI: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Vivek Kulkarni (Private)
- Partner: Laura Bennett (Finance), Michael Grant (Legal)

Workstream B — Listings + Messaging
- DRI: Soojin Lee
- Exec sponsor: Camila Reyes
- Inputs: Jordan Blake + Markus Klein (field needs)

Workstream C — Security Packet + Evidence
- Exec sponsor/sign-off: Dr. Aisha Rahman
- DRIs: Marcus Lin (SecEng controls accuracy), Olga Petrov (GRC evidence)

Workstream D — Provisioning + Console + Billing
- DRI: Ethan Park (entitlements), Chloe Martin (Console), Cole Summers (billing)
- SRE/monitoring: Rafael Mendes + Allison Grant

Workstream E — Docs + Support Readiness
- DRI: Elliot Price (Docs), Dev Patel (Support), Jasmine Liu (CS)

Speaker notes:
- If you’re unsure where you fit, pick the workstream and we’ll add you to the weekly.


Slide 8 — Timeline (target 8–10 weeks)
Week 1–2: Discovery & requirements
- Finalize SKU taxonomy + naming rules
- Inventory listing gaps (AWS vs GCP requirements)
- Identify security review requirements + evidence needed

Week 2–6: Build & draft
- Implement entitlement mapping/webhook improvements
- Draft listing copy + screenshots
- Draft security packet + internal review

Week 5–8: Review & submission
- Internal approvals (Product/Finance/Legal/Security)
- AWS + GCP submission + iteration cycles

Week 8–10: Launch & stabilization
- Publish listings
- Monitor entitlement lag + error rates
- Support playbooks live; post-launch retro + metrics review

Speaker notes:
- Review lead times are the biggest unknown; we’ll manage with early submission + rapid turnarounds.


Slide 9 — Key milestones + acceptance criteria
Milestone 1: SKU taxonomy “locked”
- Naming is consistent across AWS, GCP, Console UI, and billing invoice strings
- Upgrade/downgrade policy defined for marketplace buyers

Milestone 2: Security packet approved
- Security claims reviewed and signed off (Aisha/Marcus/Olga)
- Evidence index ready with NDA/disclaimer guidance

Milestone 3: Onboarding flow passes E2E
- Purchase → entitlement active within SLO (target: minutes, not hours)
- Org linking is self-serve with clear UX + error states
- Idempotent processing + audit logs verified

Milestone 4: Launch readiness
- Support macros + escalation on-call schedule
- Dashboards + alerts in place (webhook failures, entitlement lag, provisioning error rate)
- Field enablement complete (FAQ + SKU chooser + talk track)


Slide 10 — Metrics (how we’ll know it worked)
Marketplace sourcing + conversion
- # marketplace leads (AWS/GCP) → activated orgs
- Activation time from purchase to first successful API call
- Drop-off points (purchase → entitlement → org link → first token)

Operational quality
- Entitlement lag p50/p95
- Webhook failure rate + retry success
- Provisioning error rate (region mismatch, wrong org, missing linking)

Business
- Marketplace-sourced pipeline ($) and closed-won ($)
- % of enterprise deals that can close via marketplace when requested

Speaker notes:
- We’ll add lightweight attribution + funnel tracking; Ben Carter will coordinate UTMs + HubSpot routing.


Slide 11 — Risks + mitigations
Risk: Marketplace review lead times + shifting requirements
- Mitigation: pre-flight checklist, early submission, dedicated response SLA, clear owners for partner feedback

Risk: SKU naming drift across systems
- Mitigation: ADR + single source mapping sheet; block launch if invoice strings don’t match naming

Risk: Security language over-promises / inconsistency across docs/listings
- Mitigation: security “approved language” blocks; final review required before submission

Risk: Entitlement activation delays create poor buyer experience and revenue leakage
- Mitigation: idempotency + retries, monitoring + alerts, support escalation, backfill tooling

Risk: GCP vs AWS format differences cause duplicate work / confusion
- Mitigation: shared messaging framework + platform-specific sections; docs compare page


Slide 12 — Decision points we need in week 1–2
Packaging decisions
- Which add-ons are separate line items vs included by default (compliance, retention, premium SLA)
- Dedicated vs Private SKU granularity (bundle vs split; regional variants)

Policy decisions
- Upgrade/downgrade rules for marketplace customers (timing, proration, approval paths)
- Discounting constraints + when to route to direct contract

Technical decisions
- Canonical entitlement IDs + backward compatibility for existing buyers
- Region mismatch handling (strict block vs guided resolution vs auto-routing where allowed)

Speaker notes:
- We’ll capture these decisions in an ADR and update the mapping sheet to avoid last-minute drift.


Slide 13 — RACI (simplified)

Slide 14 — Comms + operating cadence
Weekly cadences
- Marketplace Refresh Weekly (cross-functional): status, blockers, partner feedback triage
- Workstream standups (as needed): Eng/DX, Security/GRC, GTM/PMM

Artifacts
- Single tracker: marketplace review checklist + milestone dates
- Partner feedback log: AWS/GCP requested changes, owners, due dates
- Mapping sheet: SKU IDs ↔ internal plans ↔ entitlements ↔ billing meters

Escalation path
- Partner review blockers: Partnerships/Marketplace owner(s) + Talia
- Security wording disputes: Marcus → Aisha for final decision
- Launch go/no-go: Evelyn Hart + workstream DRIs


Slide 15 — Immediate next steps (this week)
By EOW
- Confirm DRIs and meeting cadence (Talia)
- Share first cut SKU taxonomy + naming rules for review (Nikhil/Lauren/Vivek)
- Establish “approved security language” doc + disclaimer guidance (Marcus/Olga)
- Start screenshot inventory + owners + redaction needs (Soojin + Design)
- Engineering: finalize acceptance criteria for purchase→provision and instrumentation plan (Ethan + Rafael)

Open asks
- Sales/SE: top 10 objections + required FAQ additions (Jordan/Markus)
- Support/CS: top recurring marketplace ticket patterns + desired macros (Dev/Jasmine)

Speaker notes:
- Please send edits async; we’ll roll them into the PRD + checklist. Goal is to be submission-ready quickly, then iterate with partner feedback.
